**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

The Agreement has no convenience-termination right for either party. Section 9 covers only cause-based grounds (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 security/SLA/law/IP failures), and the other exits (6.2 failed acceptance, 19.4 warranty, 27.3 force majeure) are all remedy-triggered. Meanwhile Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term and Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely in walk-away territory under this rule.

Vendor also lacks a convenience right, which suits us, so the redline is one-sided in our favour only to the extent the playbook requires.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):** new Section 9.4 after 9.3 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right, in whole or in part, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, release from further minimum-commitment obligations for the terminated Services (expressly notwithstanding Section 2.1), and confirmation that Vendor has no mid-term convenience exit. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback if needed.
